title: Representations of an acyclic quiver
notes: A quiver is called a directed graph without cycles; \(M(\Lambda,\Omega)\) is its representation category.
statement: For a finite quiver \(Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) with no oriented cycles over a field \(k\), let \(\operatorname{rep}_kQ\) consist of finite-dimensional vertex spaces and linear arrow maps. It is an abelian hereditary category, equivalent to finite-dimensional modules over \(kQ\).
reconstruction: Finiteness, the coefficient field, and oriented rather than undirected cycles are made explicit.
fate: This is the framework of \citet[\S1]{bernsteingelfandponomarev1973coxeter}; the derived-category report uses it in \citet[\S1]{parthasarathy1988tstructures}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Orientation independence and its graph hypothesis
notes: The lemma says \(\mathcal D(\Lambda,\Omega_1)\simeq\mathcal D(\Lambda,\Omega_2)\) for different orientations, with reflections as proof.
statement: A reflection at a source or sink induces an equivalence of bounded derived categories. Hence orientations joined by such reflections have equivalent categories; in particular this holds for any two orientations of a finite tree, including every Dynkin tree.
reconstruction: The tree or reflection-equivalence hypothesis is essential; the drawing alone does not establish it.
fate: \citet[Propositions~1.4 and~1.6]{parthasarathy1988tstructures} constructs the derived reflection equivalences from BGP functors. An unrestricted assertion for all acyclic orientations of an arbitrary graph is not supplied by this argument. Derived equivalence under tilting was already proved in \citet[\S1.7, Corollary, p.~344]{happel1987derived}, published in 1987 after an Ottawa 1984 announcement; applied to a source/sink reflection, it supplies the pre-talk derived-category formulation.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: derived reflection invariance is established; the notebook' s unrestricted orientation wording should not be used as a theorem.

title: Hearts with the same derived category
notes: Find abelian subcategories \(\mathcal A\subset\mathcal D\) with \(\mathcal D^\ell(\mathcal A)=\mathcal D\); the notes say all are found and characterized by Dynkin graphs.
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field and Q a finite acyclic quiver. Describe bounded t-structures on \(D^b(\operatorname{rep}_kQ)\) whose heart \(\mathcal A\) is a finite-length abelian k-category with a projective generator and finite-dimensional Hom spaces, and whose realization functor \(D^b(\mathcal A)\to D^b(\operatorname{rep}_kQ)\) is an equivalence.
reconstruction: The superscript is read as bounded derived category, and abelian subcategory is interpreted as a heart. The stated finiteness conditions prevent a claim about arbitrary embedded abelian categories.
fate: \citet[Theorems~3.3, 7.1 and~8.5]{parthasarathy1988tstructures} gives a criterion for the specified t-structure data, relates the constructed hearts to iterated tilted algebras, and proves completeness in the Dynkin case. It was received 15 February 1988, revised 13 May, and published in December 1988 by Parthasarathy, whose work Kapranov reports here; receipt alone does not establish public pre-talk circulation of the criterion. The Dynkin algebra classification itself was already \citet[Theorem~5.12, p.~358]{happel1987derived}, published in 1987 after an Ottawa 1984 announcement. Thus the later publication match is the explicit heart-realization approach, not a claim that the Dynkin classification first appeared in 1988. The notebook blanket sentence is broader than either precise formulation.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the identified finite-type/iterated-tilting classification is established; an unrestricted classification is not asserted.

title: A source reflection retains a two-term complex
notes: At a source \(\alpha\), replace \(V_\alpha\) by the cokernel of \(V_\alpha\to\bigoplus_{\alpha\to\beta}V_\beta\); vectors killed by every arrow are lost, so retain the map as a complex.
statement: The ordinary reflection uses that cokernel and reverses the incident arrows. Its total derived functor uses the two-term complex, with a degree convention fixed once, and preserves the kernel information. This gives the source reflection equivalence.
reconstruction: The vertex is required to be a source and the cone shift is conventional.
fate: BGP\textquotesingle s source/sink functors appear in \citet[\S1]{bernsteingelfandponomarev1973coxeter}; the derived construction is explicit in \citet[\S1, Proposition~1.6]{parthasarathy1988tstructures}. Derived equivalence under tilting was already proved in \citet[\S1.7, Corollary, p.~344]{happel1987derived}, published in 1987 after an Ottawa 1984 announcement; applied to a source/sink reflection, it supplies the pre-talk derived-category formulation.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Derived categories as a language for projective bundles
notes: Gelfand says classification of vector bundles on \(\mathbb{CP}^n\) can only be done in the language of derived categories.
statement: An established precise tool is the exceptional collection \((\mathcal O,\mathcal O(1),\ldots,\mathcal O(n))\) on \(\mathbb P^n\) and the resulting resolution of coherent sheaves by explicit complexes. This does not prove the literal exclusivity of a mathematical language or classify all bundles.
reconstruction: The resolution is an illustrative reconstruction of the method, not an assertion that Gelfand stated a classification theorem.
fate: \citet{beilinson1978coherent} supplies the relevant pre-1988 construction. The word only is methodological emphasis rather than a theorem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The unexplained three-versus-four distinction
notes: Parthasarathy is said to answer when the derived category coincides with this one: for three, but not for four.
statement: No definite equivalence assertion is reconstructible: the category being compared and the meaning of three or four are not specified beyond the adjacent star diagram.
fate: The explicit source-star construction and the Dynkin classification in \citet[\S\S1,8]{parthasarathy1988tstructures} explain possible background, but do not license an exact numerical theorem from this sentence.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: unidentified at the level of an exact mathematical statement.

title: Linear independence as a matroid
notes: Gelfand gives linearly independent systems of vectors as the example of a matroid.
statement: For a finite indexed family \((v_e)_{e\in E}\) in a vector space, let \(\mathcal I=\{I\subset E:(v_e)_{e\in I}\text{ is linearly independent}\}\). Heredity and the exchange axiom make \((E,\mathcal I)\) a matroid.
fate: This is the elementary representable-matroid example in \citet[opening definitions]{oxleybriefly}. Compare the matroid/lattice occurrence 1985-658.12; no new problem is posed here.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Rado transversals and the induced rank formula
notes: For a relation \(\varphi\subset M_1\times M_2\), the asserted rank is \(r_2(A)=\min_{B\subset A}(r_1(\varphi(B))+|A-B|)\).
statement: Let \(M_1\) be a finite matroid and \(M_2\) finite. A subset \(I\subset M_2\) is independent when it admits distinct representatives in \(M_1\), related to its elements by \(\varphi\), that form an independent set of the first matroid. These sets form a matroid, and the displayed minimum is its rank on \(A\).
reconstruction: Finite ground sets and the independent-transversal definition are supplied explicitly.
fate: The independence-transversal theorem is \citet{rado1942independence}; Hall\textquotesingle s special case predates it. The publisher-deposited Crossref metadata for Rado were opened and checked; the full original theorem was not successfully opened in this run.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Hall's marriage theorem and the free-matroid reduction
notes: The union condition for sets \(B(n)\subset M\) yields an injection \(f:N\to M\); the notes write \(f(n)\subset B(n)\) and declare all subsets of \(N\) independent.
statement: For finite \(N\), an injection satisfying \(f(n)\in B(n)\) exists iff \(|\bigcup_{n\in K}B(n)|\geq|K|\) for every \(K\subset N\). To derive this from Rado with representatives in \(M\), use the free matroid on \(M\), whose rank is cardinality.
reconstruction: Membership replaces subset inclusion, and the free matroid belongs on the representative ground set \(M\).
fate: \citet[Theorem~1, pp.~27--29]{hall1935representatives} proves precisely this condition; the paper was received and read in April 1934 and published in 1935.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: An algorithmic proof of the marriage theorem
notes: There is a proof containing an algorithm.
statement: For a finite bipartite graph, start with a matching and repeatedly augment along alternating paths. If no augmenting path exists while a left vertex is unmatched, its alternating reachable sets violate Hall\textquotesingle s condition. Thus the procedure finds a complete left matching under that condition.
reconstruction: The notes do not name a running time or a particular implementation; no algorithmic novelty is inferred.
fate: \citet[proof of Theorem~1]{hall1935representatives} gives a constructive replacement argument. The augmenting-path formulation is an explicit modern reconstruction of the terse algorithmic remark.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: A common system of left and right coset representatives
notes: A finite subgroup has representatives that work simultaneously for its left and right cosets; the statement is attributed to Birkhoff.
statement: If \(H\leq G\) and \(G\) is finite, there is a set meeting each left coset and each right coset of \(H\) once. More generally finite \(H\) admits such a transversal in arbitrary \(G\), by applying the finite equal-block matching argument within each double coset and choosing these transversals.
reconstruction: For infinite \(G\), each double coset has equally many left and right cosets because \(H\) is finite; a choice of the finite matchings is used.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3 and its equal-size corollary, pp.~29--30]{hall1935representatives} supplies the partition theorem; its application to cosets is immediate. Hall credits the equal-block result to Konig, so the notebook\textquotesingle s attribution is not independently confirmed.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The parallel postulate and non-Euclidean models
notes: The parallel axiom is listed as a seemingly fruitless problem that produced non-Euclidean geometry.
statement: Models of hyperbolic geometry satisfy the other standard incidence/congruence axioms but not Euclid\textquotesingle s parallel axiom; relative to the consistency of the background geometry, the axiom cannot be deduced from those remaining axioms.
reconstruction: The formal independence statement is relative to an axiom system and consistency assumption, neither specified in the remark.
fate: \citet{beltrami1869interpretation} is the opened 1869 French publication of Beltrami\textquotesingle s 1868 interpretation. This supports the mathematical endpoint, not an exhaustive causal history.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Classical construction impossibilities
notes: Angle trisection and circle quadrature are linked with the development of Galois theory.
statement: With an unmarked straightedge and compass, an arbitrary given angle cannot be trisected, and a square of the same area as a given circle cannot be constructed. The first follows from a cubic obstruction, for example trisection of \(60^\circ\); the second follows from the transcendence of \(\pi\).
reconstruction: The allowed instruments and the general rather than every-angle quantifier are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S1 and the applications]{wantzel1837constructions} treats algebraic constructibility and trisection. The two impossibilities have different proofs; quadrature is not a consequence solely of finite Galois theory. The opened publisher record verifies Lindemann\textquotesingle s 1882 paper; its original proof was not read in this run.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Fermat's equation and the later modularity proof
notes: Fermat\textquotesingle s problem is linked to Kummer\textquotesingle s ideals and algebraic geometry; Faltings appears in a marginal annotation.
statement: For every integer \(n>2\), there are no positive integers \(a,b,c\) with \(a^n+b^n=c^n\). Finiteness of rational points on a fixed genus-greater-than-one curve does not by itself prove this nonexistence statement.
reconstruction: The exact Fermat statement is the standard meaning of the named problem; the marginal Faltings attribution is not turned into a claim of a solution.
fate: \citet{wiles1995modular} establishes the semistable modularity theorem underlying the proof; the final argument was published in 1995 after the 1993 announcement and the repair with Taylor. The opened Annals record confirms publication, but the full proof was not read in this run.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Fermat' s last theorem is proved; the historical chain in the notes remains a compressed motivation.

title: Four colours and computer-assisted proof
notes: The four-colour problem is connected with computer mathematics.
statement: Every finite loopless planar graph admits a proper vertex colouring with at most four colours. The 1976 Appel--Haken proof combined unavoidable configurations with certified reducibility computations.
fate: The reducibility component was published as \citet{appelhakenkoch1977reducibility}; \citet[\S\S2--3]{gonthier2005fourcolour} later formalized the complete theorem. Fuchs returns to the proof in record 745.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The Riemann hypothesis
notes: The Riemann hypothesis is the fifth named example; no proof or strengthened formulation follows.
statement: Every zero \(\rho\) of the analytically continued Riemann zeta function with \(0<\Re\rho<1\) satisfies \(\Re\rho=1/2\).
fate: The Clay Mathematics Institute\textquotesingle s current official problem page, \citet{clay2026riemann}, still labels the problem unsolved. No narrower new question or mechanism is present in these notes.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: open; no seminar-specific partial result is claimed.
worth: The famous conjecture is worth research in general, but this occurrence offers no bounded route for a new contribution in the present chapter.

title: Exceptional bundles and ordered exceptional collections
notes: For bundles \(E_1,E_2,E_3\) on \(\mathbb P^2\), the notes impose scalar endomorphisms, vanishing positive self-Ext, and backward Ext vanishing.
statement: An object \(E\in D^b(\operatorname{Coh}X)\) is exceptional when \(\operatorname{Hom}(E,E)=k\) and \(\operatorname{Ext}^p(E,E)=0\) for \(p\ne0\). An ordered exceptional collection satisfies \(\operatorname{Ext}^p(E_j,E_i)=0\) for every \(p\) and \(j>i\). Here the objects are algebraic vector bundles on \(\mathbb P^2\).
reconstruction: The general derived definition includes all integer shifts; for vector bundles on the plane only Ext degrees 0,1,2 can occur.
fate: \citet[\S1]{rudakov1988markov} states the bundle framework, already developed by the time of the talk. The corresponding 1987 projective-space paper is \citet{gorodentsevrudakov1987exceptional}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Exceptional ranks satisfy the Markov equation
notes: The ranks \(x_1,x_2,x_3\) of the exceptional triple satisfy \(x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2=3x_1x_2x_3\).
statement: For a full exceptional triple of vector bundles on \(\mathbb P^2\), its positive ranks form a positive integer solution of the Markov equation.
reconstruction: Fullness and positive ranks are stated explicitly; this is not a rank equation for arbitrary triples of exceptional bundles.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3.2]{rudakov1988markov} gives the rank identity. The Russian original appeared in 1988, volume 52, issue 1; the English translation in 1989. Its submission was in April 1986.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Realization of positive Markov triples by bundles
notes: Conversely, the notes say every integer solution is obtained.
statement: Every positive integer Markov triple is realized by the ranks of an exceptional triple of bundles on \(\mathbb P^2\), obtained from the standard triple by the appropriate mutations and ordering conventions. Zero or negative integral solutions are not positive bundle ranks.
reconstruction: The word integer is restricted to positive integer, as required by ranks.
fate: \citet[Introduction and Theorem~4.2]{rudakov1988markov} constructs the Markov tree of adjacent exceptional bundles. This does not assert the separate Markov uniqueness conjecture that a largest entry determines the triple.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Mutation and the braid action on the plane
notes: The braid group acts on exceptional triples, transitively in the plane case.
statement: Left and right mutations of adjacent exceptional objects obey the braid relation and act on full exceptional collections. For the plane, the bundle/helix formulation produces the exceptional triples from a standard helix, with the usual shifts and simultaneous line-bundle twists accounted for.
reconstruction: The action is naturally on derived exceptional collections; a statement restricted to bundles requires the helix conventions, which the notes suppress.
fate: \citet{gorodentsevrudakov1987exceptional} is the 1987 projective-space source; \citet[\S\S3--4]{rudakov1988markov} gives the explicit plane reconstruction corresponding to Markov moves.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Exceptional quadruples on a quadric
notes: For \(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1\), exceptional quadruples also have a braid action and satisfy a more complicated Diophantine system.
statement: On the smooth quadric surface, the four line bundles \(\mathcal O,\mathcal O(1,0),\mathcal O(0,1),\mathcal O(1,1)\) generate a standard helix. Mutations construct other helices; every helix and every exceptional bundle is constructible in Rudakov\textquotesingle s precise sense.
reconstruction: The standard helix and the exact later theorems are supplied as a bounded publication match; they do not reconstruct all numerical equations in the notebook.
fate: \citet[Theorems~7.1 and~10.1]{rudakov1988quadric} proves these construction results in the Russian paper published in issue 4 of 1988, translated in 1989. The English original received-date line reads 6 July 1986. This is a precise later result, not identification of an omitted numerical system.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The unspecified converse for quadric numerical data
notes: The notes say it has not been proved that all solutions of the quadric system arise from exceptional quadruples.
statement: An exact arithmetic realization question cannot be recovered, because neither the system nor its positivity, integrality and Chern-class restrictions is written.
fate: \citet[\S\S5--7 and closing remark]{rudakov1988quadric} distinguishes helix construction, symmetric numerical equations, and a question about extending exceptional pairs. None can be silently substituted for the unnamed system here.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the exact notebook question is unidentified; it is not indexed as an open numerical problem.

title: Mutation of collections on higher projective spaces
notes: For \(\mathbb P^n\), take \(n+1\) bundles with the same exceptional conditions; a braid group again acts.
statement: Mutations act on ordered full exceptional collections of length \(n+1\) in \(D^b(\operatorname{Coh}\mathbb P^n)\). The standard line-bundle collection is an example. This statement does not claim transitivity on all collections or classification of all vector bundles when \(n>2\).
fate: The pre-talk source is \citet{gorodentsevrudakov1987exceptional}; its bibliographic record was opened. The construction is consistent with the explicit mutation formalism in \citet[\S2]{rudakov1988quadric}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Finite, tame, and wild representation problems
notes: Gelfand distinguishes no parameters, one parameter, and at least two parameters, comparing the last with classifying pairs of matrices.
statement: For a fixed finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field, finite representation type means finitely many indecomposable isomorphism classes; tame type permits finitely many one-parameter families in each dimension, with finitely many exceptions; wildness means that the problem of modules over the free algebra in two generators embeds in the representation problem. A raw count of parameters does not define these alternatives.
reconstruction: The standard representation-theoretic meanings replace the informal parameter count.
fate: For quivers, the finite/Dynkin and extended-Dynkin examples already occur in 1972-277.8 and 1972-278.9. \citet{bernsteingelfandponomarev1973coxeter} supplies the finite-type setting. The remark is not a proof of a general dichotomy theorem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: An open orbit is not automatic in a wild problem
notes: Gelfand says an unsolvable classification always contains a solvable part, adding an open orbit.
statement: Existence of a dense open orbit is a separate geometric condition. In simultaneous conjugation of pairs of \(n\times n\) complex matrices, the invariant \(\operatorname{tr}(A)\) varies, so no orbit can be dense in the full affine space of pairs. This already refutes an unconditional open-orbit assertion.
reconstruction: \ours{} The text is read literally as claiming an open orbit in the original representation space; a more restricted stratum could behave differently.
fate: This is an elementary editorial check: a polynomial invariant is constant on an orbit and its closure. No external classification theorem is needed. The BGP finite-type examples give context only.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: false without a specified stratum or additional hypotheses.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Self-Ext vanishing and infinitesimal rigidity
notes: \(\operatorname{Ext}^1(E,E)=0\) is interpreted as rigidity of a vector bundle.
statement: For a vector bundle on a proper scheme over a field, first-order deformations over the dual numbers are parametrized by \(\operatorname{Ext}^1(E,E)\). Its vanishing implies infinitesimal rigidity; the stronger assertion of a unique global isomorphism class does not follow.
reconstruction: The meaning of rigidity is restricted to infinitesimal deformations, with the usual fixed base and deformation functor.
fate: The deformation-free exceptional-bundle setting is explicit in \citet[Introduction and \S1]{rudakov1988markov}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Exceptional pairs require exceptional individual objects
notes: A pair is called exceptional if \(\operatorname{Ext}^j(F,E)=0\); the individual conditions are not repeated.
statement: An exceptional pair \((E,F)\) consists of two exceptional objects and has \(\operatorname{RHom}(F,E)=0\). Backward orthogonality alone is insufficient to imply either object is exceptional.
reconstruction: The individual scalar-endomorphism and self-Ext conditions are explicitly reinstated.
fate: \citet[\S2]{rudakov1988quadric} gives the admissible/exceptional pair formalism; the earlier individual conditions on P001448 provide likely context, but must be restored when this item is read alone.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The kernel mutation has the wrong pair order in the notes
notes: The sequence \(0\to R\to E\otimes\operatorname{Hom}(E,F)\to F\) is followed by the assertion that \((F,R)\) is exceptional.
statement: For an exceptional pair with \(\operatorname{RHom}(E,F)\) concentrated in degree zero and surjective evaluation, the kernel \(R\) gives the left mutation, with the appropriate shift convention. The resulting exceptional pair is \((R,E)\), not \((F,R)\). In general use the distinguished triangle \(L_EF\to\operatorname{RHom}(E,F)\otimes E\to F\to L_EF[1]\).
reconstruction: \ours{} Surjectivity and the strong-pair hypothesis are needed for a kernel bundle; the triangle supplies the general derived construction.
fate: \citet[\S2]{rudakov1988quadric} gives left/right mutation. A direct check on \(\mathbb P^1\), \(E=\mathcal O\), \(F=\mathcal O(1)\), has \(R=\mathcal O(-1)\) and \(\operatorname{Hom}(R,F)\ne0\), contradicting the displayed pair in the notebook.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the standard mutation is established; the literal order in the source is false.

title: Braid relations and the quiver-reflection analogy
notes: Mutation gives the braid-group action; Gelfand recalls BGP and recommends studying quiver representations and derived categories for spectral theory.
statement: Adjacent mutations on exceptional collections satisfy \(\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\), with distant generators commuting. BGP reflections provide a related, but differently defined, transformation of quiver representations.
reconstruction: The braid relation is stated for the derived mutation operations; the analogy is not an identification of the two actions.
fate: \citet[\S2, Proposition~2.1 and the reconstruction formalism]{rudakov1988quadric} treats mutations; \citet[\S1]{bernsteingelfandponomarev1973coxeter} is the earlier reflection construction. The recommendation for spectral theory states no further definite theorem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Gelfand's geometric configuration question
notes: Before the perverse-sheaf exposition, Gelfand asks about regions/configurations and Siegel domains, with a drawing in the real projective plane.
statement: The invariant, parameter space, equivalence relation and intended assertion are not specified well enough to formulate a definite classification problem.
fate: The neighbouring microlocal discussion does not supply the missing data. No exact publication is identified, and no open problem is inferred from a topic-level resemblance.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: unidentified as a mathematical question.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Constructible sheaves and complexes
notes: A sheaf is locally constant of finite rank on each stratum; for a complex the condition is on its cohomology sheaves, not on its terms.
statement: For a complex algebraic variety with a finite algebraic Whitney stratification \(\mathcal S\), \(D^b_{\mathcal S}(X;k)\) consists of bounded sheaf complexes whose cohomology restricts to finite-rank local systems on every stratum. Analytic versions use locally finite stratifications.
reconstruction: Boundedness, coefficients, Whitney regularity and finiteness conventions are supplied.
fate: \citet[Chapter~8]{kashiwaraschapira1985microlocal} treats the constructibility conditions. The notebook correctly distinguishes cohomological constructibility from a particular complex of representatives.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Singular support requires uniform local tests
notes: A nonzero covector is excluded from \(SS(\mathcal F)\) when a relative cohomology group for a function with that differential vanishes; the notes say the choice of function does not matter.
statement: For a bounded constructible complex on a real manifold, \((x,\xi)\notin SS(F)\) means there is an open conic neighbourhood on which all local cohomology tests \((R\Gamma_{\{\phi\geq\phi(y)\}}F)_y\) vanish whenever \((y,d\phi_y)\) lies in that neighbourhood. Holomorphic Morse tests describe the corresponding complex-constructible microsupport, with their normalizations.
reconstruction: The precise real-test definition is supplied to avoid interpreting a schematic single-function test as an invariant definition.
fate: The uniform-neighbourhood condition is in \citet[Definition~0.1 and \S3.1]{kashiwaraschapira1985microlocal}. Vanishing for a single arbitrary chosen function is not the complete definition.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The zero-section part of singular support
notes: If the complex is nonzero, the entire zero section is added; an acyclic complex has empty singular support.
statement: One has \(SS(F)\cap T_X^*X=\operatorname{supp}(F)\), where the right side is embedded as zero covectors. Thus \(SS(0)=\varnothing\), but a nonzero skyscraper sheaf does not contain zero covectors over other points.
reconstruction: \ours{}
fate: \citet[\S3.1, basic properties of microsupport]{kashiwaraschapira1985microlocal} gives the support relation. The skyscraper example on P001452 itself detects the error.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the support-restricted statement is standard; the unconditional addition of the zero section is false.

title: Complex constructibility gives a conic Lagrangian support
notes: \(SS(F)\) is an analytic conic Lagrangian set with finitely many irreducible components; ideal involutivity is presented as equivalent.
statement: For complex-constructible \(F\), its microsupport, identified with the complex cotangent bundle, is a closed complex-conic Lagrangian analytic subset. Components are locally finite; global finiteness follows in the finite algebraic setting. Involutivity of the ideal gives coisotropicity, and is equivalent to the Lagrangian condition only with the half-dimensional hypothesis.
reconstruction: Complex constructibility and the dimension/finiteness qualifications are made explicit.
fate: \citet[Theorem~6.4.1 and Chapter~8]{kashiwaraschapira1985microlocal} supplies involutivity and the constructible Lagrangian characterization.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Irreducible conic Lagrangians are conormal closures
notes: An irreducible conic Lagrangian \(Y\subset T^*X\) is \(N^*Z\) for \(Z=\pi(Y)\), with closure over the smooth locus understood.
statement: In the algebraic setting, a closed irreducible conic Lagrangian subset is the closure of \(T^*_{Z_{\mathrm{sm}}}X\) for the irreducible subvariety \(Z=\overline{\pi(Y)}\). The analytic assertion is local. This follows by annihilating tangent vectors to a generic smooth image under the canonical symplectic form and comparing dimensions.
reconstruction: Closedness, algebraic/local analytic context and closure of the image are specified.
fate: This is the conormal geometry underlying \citet[Chapter~8]{kashiwaraschapira1985microlocal}. The argument and the closure conventions are elementary reconstruction of the lemma as stated.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Morse transversality to a singular support
notes: The graph of \(df\) must meet \(Y\) only at smooth points and transversely; examples are the zero section and a smooth conormal.
statement: For a holomorphic function \(f\) and conic Lagrangian \(Y\), a microlocal Morse point is a transverse intersection of \(\Gamma_{df}\) with \(Y_{\mathrm{sm}}\), away from the singular part of \(Y\). For \(Y=T_X^*X\) this is an ordinary nondegenerate critical point; for \(Y=T_Z^*X\) with smooth \(Z\), it is a nondegenerate critical point of \(f|_Z\).
reconstruction: The criterion is local at an isolated transverse intersection, not a demand that a global function exist with every required property.
fate: This is the test-function construction used in \citet[Introduction and \S1]{gelfandmacphersonvilonen2005microlocal}, building on the earlier microlocal theory. The crossed-out extra demand \(df\ne0\) is not part of the general conormal criterion.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Perversity detected by Morse groups
notes: All Morse relative hypercohomology groups must occur in degree zero; a parenthetical remark instead says first degree.
statement: With the convention that \(k_X[\dim_{\mathbb C}X]\) is perverse, a constructible bounded complex is perverse exactly when its normalized local Morse groups are concentrated in degree zero. For an isolated Morse test, these can be represented by \(\mathbb H^j(B,B\cap f^{-1}(\varepsilon);F)\), after fixing the vanishing-cycle shift convention.
reconstruction: The normalized Morse functor rather than an unlabelled cone fixes the degree convention.
fate: \citet[Theorem~9.5.2 and Introduction]{kashiwaraschapira1985microlocal} gives the microlocal characterization. The degree-one parenthesis can reflect the unshifted vanishing-cycle cone, and cannot coexist literally with degree zero without specifying the shift.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Basic perverse sheaves and the closed-embedding hypothesis
notes: Examples are a skyscraper, \(\mathbb C_X[n]\), and \(\mathbb C_Z[\dim Z]\) extended by zero from a smooth subset, or an intersection-cohomology complex.
statement: A finite-dimensional skyscraper is perverse. On a smooth complex \(n\)-fold a local system shifted by \(n\) is perverse. For a closed smooth embedding \(i:Z\hookrightarrow X\), \(i_*L[\dim Z]\) is perverse. For an arbitrary open or locally closed embedding, ordinary extension by zero need not be perverse; intermediate extension is the appropriate canonical construction.
reconstruction: Closedness is restored to the zero-extension example; the singular case uses intersection cohomology rather than a constant sheaf.
fate: \citet[Theorem~9.5.2]{kashiwaraschapira1985microlocal} gives the perverse framework, and \citet{goreskymacpherson1983intersection} is the intersection-cohomology source.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Singular support does not canonically recover every stratum
notes: An explicitly approximate remark identifies strata with projections of irreducible components of \(SS(F)\).
statement: The projections recover certain closed singular-support loci, not a unique stratification. A compatible Whitney stratification may be refined without changing \(F\) or \(SS(F)\); even the constant sheaf admits many such refinements.
reconstruction: \ours{} The notebook already flags the assertion as approximate; its strongest literal interpretation is rejected.
fate: \citet[Chapter~8]{kashiwaraschapira1985microlocal} relates constructibility to unions of conormals, which is weaker than a unique reconstruction of the chosen strata.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: only the conormal-support relation is valid; no canonical full stratification follows.

title: Morse groups form a microlocal local system with a twist
notes: At a smooth covector \(z\), define \(\Phi(F)_z=H^0(U,f^{-1}(\varepsilon);F)\) for \(df=z\), claiming no dependence on \(f\).
statement: On the smooth locus of a fixed singular support, normalized Morse data vary locally constantly after accounting for the Maslov/orientation data of the test-function Hessian. The natural object is a twisted local system (or a local system on the appropriate bundle of Morse data), not canonically an untwisted local system from the covector alone.
reconstruction: The twisting is a modern clarification, not wording supplied by the notebook.
fate: \citet[\S1, the bundle of test Lagrangians and Maslov data]{gelfandmacphersonvilonen2005microlocal} makes the suppressed structure explicit. Its preprint appeared in September 2005; the 1988 talk already attributes the programme to the same three authors.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Configurations, reducibility, and unavoidability
notes: A configuration is a triangulated disc; an unavoidable collection occurs in every triangulation, and a reducible member cannot occur in a smallest counterexample.
statement: In a finite simple plane triangulation, a configuration specifies a finite near-triangulation together with the required degrees of its internal vertices and a boundary ring. Reducibility means that an occurrence can be replaced by a smaller graph whose four-colouring can be lifted, possibly using Kempe changes. An unavoidable set is one occurring in every triangulation of the relevant reduced class.
reconstruction: Degree and boundary data and the relevant class of minimal counterexamples are restored.
fate: \citet[\S3]{gonthier2005fourcolour} states the established proof structure, already present in the 1977 Appel--Haken proof. An arbitrary disc triangulation without embedding and degree data is not the complete configuration specification.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: An unavoidable reducible family proves four-colourability
notes: The main idea is to combine the two definitions and induct on the number of vertices.
statement: If every minimal non-four-colourable plane triangulation contains a member of a fixed family, and every member is reducible, no minimal counterexample exists. After deleting duplicate edges, a finite loopless planar graph with at least three vertices extends to a simple plane triangulation; smaller graphs are immediate. Restricting a four-colouring yields the theorem.
fate: The proof scheme was realized in \citet{appelhakenkoch1977reducibility}; \citet[\S3, parts I--II]{gonthier2005fourcolour} states its formalized version.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The cosine addition identity as a spherical-function example
notes: Gelfand says his spherical-function theory arose from \(\cos(\alpha+\beta)+\cos(\alpha-\beta)=2\cos\alpha\cos\beta\), using translations and reflections of the line.
statement: For \(G=\mathbb R\rtimes\{\pm1\}\), \(K=\{\pm1\}\), the functions \(\varphi_t(x)=\cos(tx)\) are normalized \(K\)-bi-invariant spherical functions and satisfy \(\frac12[\varphi_t(x+y)+\varphi_t(x-y)]=\varphi_t(x)\varphi_t(y)\). This is a concrete product-formula model.
reconstruction: The parameter t, subgroup K and normalized averaging are explicit reconstruction of the stated example.
fate: The general spherical-function setting is represented by \citet{berezingelfand1956spherical}; the displayed semidirect-product calculation directly verifies the specific example. The personal account of invention is not independently checked.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Degree-four vertices are reducible by a Kempe argument
notes: For four neighbours with all four colours, either the 1--3 Kempe path is absent, or its planar separation prevents a 2--4 path; a colour swap frees a colour.
statement: In a plane triangulation, a vertex of degree four cannot belong to a minimal non-four-colourable graph. Remove it and colour the smaller graph. If the four cyclic neighbours use four different colours, disjoint alternating 1--3 and 2--4 connecting paths cannot both exist in the punctured plane; swap on a component of one colour pair and extend the colouring.
reconstruction: The cyclic order and planarity are the essential topological hypotheses.
fate: \citet[\S3, the square case]{gonthier2005fourcolour} records this classical Kempe reduction. The valid degree-four argument does not validate Kempe\textquotesingle s failed degree-five argument.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Boundary colourings and Kempe closure
notes: Some boundary colourings extend into a configuration, others do not; a computer searches for recolourings as in the previous example.
statement: For a fixed finite ring configuration, enumerate proper four-colourings of the ring and the subset extendible through the interior. Reducibility tests combine this finite data with the permitted noncrossing Kempe-chain pairing information from the exterior. Arbitrary swaps of boundary colours without such compatibility do not establish reducibility.
reconstruction: The exterior noncrossing compatibility, not spelled out in the sketch, is essential.
fate: \citet[\S5.2]{gonthier2005fourcolour} formalizes the Kempe-chain and reducibility calculation. The 1977 proof already used finite reducibility algorithms; the later proof verifies a specific implementation.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The drawn configuration is the Birkhoff diamond
notes: The scan draws a hexagonal ring around four interior vertices and calls it reducible, adding that Fuchs could not prove it.
statement: The four interior vertices span two triangles sharing an edge, and each has degree five in the completed patch. Together with the six-vertex boundary this is the free completion of the Birkhoff diamond, a reducible configuration.
reconstruction: Identification uses the graph incidence and degree-five internal vertices visible in the scan; no missing proof is attributed to Fuchs.
fate: The scan was compared with the structural description in \citet[\S3, part g, pp.~7--8]{gonthier2005fourcolour}. Its reducibility is a classical pre-1988 result, not a new unresolved problem; the attribution to the name Birkhoff is editorial.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: A parallel program for a fixed reducibility test
notes: Gelfand\textquotesingle s numbered problem asks for a program determining reducibility on a parallel computer.
statement: Given a finite ring configuration, implement a specified sound finite reducibility test based on boundary colourings and compatible Kempe data, allowing independent colourings/configurations to be processed in parallel. No machine model, complexity bound or completeness criterion for all notions of reducibility is stated.
reconstruction: A specified finite sufficient test is distinguished from universal semantic reducibility; without that distinction the requested input/output problem is ambiguous.
fate: Computer reducibility tests already existed in 1977, and \citet[\S5.2]{gonthier2005fourcolour} later gives a formally checked implementation. That is only a partial match: this search did not identify a publication answering Gelfand\textquotesingle s exact parallel-program request. Finite enumeration itself can be parallelized, so the text does not define a new unsolved mathematical decision problem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the finite testing method and verified implementations are established; no exact historical parallel implementation has been identified.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Euler curvature and a first unavoidable set
notes: Using \(V-E+F=2\), \(2E=\sum i\nu_i\), \(3F=2E\), the notes derive \(\sum(6-i)\nu_i=12\), so a degree-three, four or five vertex exists.
statement: For a finite simple triangulation of the sphere with at least four vertices, \(\sum_v(6-\deg v)=12\). Its minimum degree is at most five. Degree-three and degree-four reduction therefore leaves minimum degree at least five in any minimal counterexample.
reconstruction: Sphere topology, simplicity and the small-size exclusion justify the degree range.
fate: This is the Euler-counting step recalled in \citet[\S3]{gonthier2005fourcolour}. The numerical identity follows directly from the three displayed counts and does not depend on computation.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Discharging preserves the total charge
notes: Assign charge \(60(6-i)\) to degree i, redistribute 30 along specified edges, and seek a contradiction by making every final charge nonpositive.
statement: The initial charge sum is \(720\). Any pairwise transfer conserves it. Therefore, if absence of a finite configuration family forces every final charge to be nonpositive under a fully specified set of transfer rules, that family is unavoidable. The single sample rule in the notes does not by itself prove the required universal implication.
reconstruction: Conservation is exact; completeness of the discharge rules is not reconstructed from the incomplete examples.
fate: \citet[\S3, discharging steps 1--2]{gonthier2005fourcolour} gives the precise proof pattern. Appel--Haken\textquotesingle s completed rule system is a much larger object than this board sketch. For the manuscript computer-time question, the contemporary digest \citet[abstract]{bernhart1977digest} reports 1200 hours for nearly 1900 configurations.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Zero microsupport detects local constancy
notes: \(SS(F)\) equals the zero section iff all cohomology sheaves are locally constant; the whole zero section is again inserted for any nonzero complex.
statement: For a constructible complex, \(SS(F)\subset T_X^*X\) iff all its cohomology sheaves are locally constant. Equality holds on connected components where the complex is nonzero. The zero complex has empty support, so equality cannot be used without the component/support qualification.
fate: \citet[\S3.1]{kashiwaraschapira1985microlocal} gives the local-constancy criterion. This is a second occurrence of the support error corrected in 1987-744.3.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Vanishing cycles as relative hypercohomology
notes: Take \(f(x)=0\), \(df_x=\nu\), and compare cohomology on a small neighbourhood with a nearby nonzero fibre; relative cohomology is defined by a cone.
statement: For a sufficiently small Milnor neighbourhood and a constructible complex adapted to \(f\), the relative derived sections \(R\Gamma(B,B\cap f^{-1}(\varepsilon);F)\) are the fibre of the restriction map. Equivalently they are its cone shifted by \(-1\). They describe local vanishing-cycle data, with the chosen convention recorded.
reconstruction: The Milnor neighbourhood, nearby regular value and shifted-cone convention are supplied.
fate: The microlocal construction in \citet[\S1]{gelfandmacphersonvilonen2005microlocal} uses these local Morse data. The cone shift matters for the degree-zero definition on the next line.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Repeated microlocal characterization of perversity
notes: A holomorphic Morse function has graph transverse to singular support; vanishing cycles occur in one degree and form a local system over the smooth support.
statement: Use isolated transverse intersections with the smooth support, degree-zero normalized Morse groups, and the Maslov-twisted local-system construction. These are the same conditions as in 1987-744.7--744.11, not a new criterion.
reconstruction: The normalization and twist from the earlier occurrence remain necessary.
fate: \citet[Theorem~9.5.2]{kashiwaraschapira1985microlocal} and \citet[\S1]{gelfandmacphersonvilonen2005microlocal} supply the precise formulations.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Reconstruct perverse sheaves from microlocal Morse data
notes: The proposed third method is a microlocal description by vanishing cycles; the report says the work solves half of the problem.
statement: Let \(X\) be a complex manifold and \(\Lambda\subset T^*X\) a specified closed complex analytic conic Lagrangian. With coefficients in \(\mathbb C\), describe the category of perverse sheaves with singular support in \(\Lambda\) by local Morse data on the smooth pieces, gluing at codimension-one loci, and explicit compatibility conditions at singular loci. A complete answer must characterize the essential image, not only embed the category faithfully.
reconstruction: The fixed-support categorical formulation and essential-image distinction make the informal reconstruction question precise; no arbitrary missing codimension-two formula is invented.
fate: \citet[Theorem~5.1 and Theorem~6.4]{gelfandmacphersonvilonen2005microlocal}, first circulated on arXiv in September 2005, proves an equivalence away from the codimension-two locus and a global fully faithful embedding in melded Morse data. \citet[Theorem~1.1]{kashiwaravilonen2014codimension}, announced in 2010 with a full preprint in 2012 and publication in 2014, proves unique extension across analytic subsets of codimension at least three in the Lagrangian support. The exact remaining task is formulated as Problem~9.3 of that paper (published p.~617): describe the conditions imposed by the codimension-two locus on the essential image. The extension theorem does not erase these conditions. \citet[Introduction]{guminov2025perverse} confirms that explicit category descriptions remain available only for restricted families.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: partially developed over complex coefficients in the explicit microlocal-data sense stated here. Kashiwara--Vilonen Problem 9.3 explicitly isolates the codimension-two essential-image question. The consulted later primary literature does not settle that general geometric description; this is a bounded search conclusion, not a claim that no categorical reconstruction theorem of any kind exists.
worth: A fixed singular support with concrete codimension-two links would make a useful bounded project, but the notebook supplies no such geometry to calculate here.

title: Holonomic differential equations and perverse solution complexes
notes: One construction uses overdetermined differential equations, a solution complex, and a Dolbeault resolution.
statement: For a regular holonomic left \(\mathcal D_X\)-module on a smooth complex n-fold, the shifted derived solution complex \(R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal D_X}(M,\mathcal O_X)[n]\) is perverse. Regular holonomic modules and complex-constructible perverse sheaves correspond contravariantly. A merely overdetermined system need not be holonomic, and an ordinary solution sheaf need not equal its derived solution complex.
reconstruction: Regular holonomicity is used for this safe exact equivalence; the notebook does not specify the module class or solution shift.
fate: \citet[main theorem, p.~1]{kashiwara1980constructible} announces the derived equivalence in the lecture of 22 April 1980; \citet{kashiwara1984riemann} is the full later publication. This predates the seminar.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Intersection cohomology and intermediate extension
notes: The Goresky--MacPherson combinatorial method extends sheaves to singular points and yields perverse sheaves.
statement: If \(j:U\hookrightarrow X\) is a smooth dense stratum of complex dimension d and \(L\) a finite-rank local system, its perverse intermediate extension \(j_{!*}L[d]\) is the intersection-cohomology complex. Arbitrary extensions across singular strata need not be perverse or canonical.
reconstruction: Intermediate extension is the precise reconstruction of the broad extension statement.
fate: The intersection-cohomology construction is \citet{goreskymacpherson1983intersection}; the extension viewpoint is also explicit in \citet{beilinson1987glue}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The finite Morse index of a geodesic
notes: The energy functional on the path space has finite negative index, equal to the number of conjugate points along the geodesic.
statement: For a geodesic segment in a smooth Riemannian manifold with fixed endpoints, the Hessian of energy has finite Morse index. It equals the sum of the multiplicities of conjugate points to the initial endpoint in the open segment; conjugacy at the final endpoint contributes to nullity, not to the negative index.
reconstruction: Fixed endpoints and the endpoint/nullity convention are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S\S1--3]{duistermaat1974morse} formulates the index in variational and Lagrangian terms. Boundary conditions and multiplicities, omitted in the board sentence, determine the exact result.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Relative grading for strongly indefinite functionals
notes: Critical points may have infinitely many positive and negative directions, but the numbers of negative directions are said to differ by a finite number; homology is counted from infinity over two.
statement: For a continuous path of self-adjoint Fredholm Hessians with invertible ends and appropriate operator-domain control, spectral flow supplies a finite relative index. Infinite positive and negative indices alone do not imply that an index difference exists. A Floer complex additionally requires compactness, transversality, coherent orientation and control of broken trajectories.
reconstruction: The Fredholm and analytic hypotheses replace subtraction of two infinite cardinalities.
fate: \citet[pp.~286--294]{atiyah1988invariants} explains the gauge-theoretic Morse picture, circulated as a 1987 lecture/preprint. \citet{floer1988instanton}, received 3 May and published June 1988, establishes the associated homology-sphere invariant. This is exposition of a programme under development, not a general theorem for arbitrary functionals.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: relative-index Floer theories are established under specific analytic hypotheses; the unrestricted formulation is invalid.

title: Relation with Donaldson invariants
notes: The striking claim is that these invariants are related to Donaldson invariants of four-manifolds; gauge fields and flat connections are drawn.
statement: The relevant functional on three-dimensional connections is Chern--Simons: its critical points are flat connections and its cylinder gradient equation is the anti-self-dual equation in four dimensions. Donaldson theory can therefore interact with the boundary Floer groups through cutting and gluing.
reconstruction: The functional is reconstructed as Chern--Simons from the named source and later continuation; Yang--Mills criticality alone would be insufficient.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--5]{atiyah1988invariants} is the named source; record 751 supplies the detailed seminar continuation. The ordinary Yang--Mills energy on a three-manifold can have nonflat critical points, so the functional in the sketch must not be identified with it without correction.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Positive and negative Fourier polarizations on the circle
notes: Gelfand recalls decomposing \(C^\infty(S^1)\) into boundary values extending inside and outside, with applications to tau-functions and semi-infinite cohomology.
statement: A smooth complex function on the circle splits into its Fourier modes \(\sum_{n\geq0}a_nz^n\) and \(\sum_{n<0}a_nz^n\). With constants included in both pieces the intersection is one-dimensional; with the negative part vanishing at infinity the direct-sum convention removes that overlap. Appropriate Sobolev completions give Hardy polarizations.
reconstruction: Boundary regularity, the constant mode and the outside normalization are made explicit.
fate: The elementary Fourier construction verifies the concrete circle example. \citet[the loop-space discussion]{atiyah1988invariants} supplies the context of relative polarizations; no new tau-function identity is asserted.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Replacing the circle by another manifold
notes: Gelfand says that remarkably the circle can be replaced by other manifolds, and postpones the explanation.
statement: No definite generalization is determined without a chosen operator or polarization, coefficient bundle, function space and intended semi-infinite invariant.
fate: The adjacent Atiyah discussion motivates spectral polarizations, but this sentence alone does not identify one. No missing theorem or open problem has been manufactured from it.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: unidentified beyond a research direction.

title: The rank-one quantum enveloping algebra and its completion
notes: The generators \(H,X^\pm\) satisfy \([H,X^\pm]=\pm2X^\pm\) and \([X^+,X^-]=\sinh(hH/2)/\sinh(h/2)\), with \(q=e^h\); powers of both \(H\) and \(q^{H/4}\) are called a vector-space basis.
statement: One coherent formulation is the h-adic algebra \(U_h(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\), topologically free over \(\mathbb C[[h]]\), with the displayed relations and PBW monomials \((X^-)^aH^b(X^+)^c\). Alternatively, for a numerical generic parameter use the algebraic Cartan generator \(K^{\pm1}\) and a PBW basis in \(X^-,K,X^+\). Exponentials are interpreted in a completion, not added as unspecified independent formal generators.
reconstruction: The completion and base ring are fixed explicitly; the notebook does not specify which algebra is meant by its basis.
fate: \citet[I, Definition~1.1 and Theorem~1.1]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi} gives the close publication match. Its series number is E-4-87 but the scanned imprint is 1988; the June 1987 recommendation does not by itself establish first public circulation. Independently, \citet[Example~6.2, p.~807]{drinfeld1987quantum}, a 1986 congress report published in 1987, gives the completed quantum enveloping algebra and symmetric coproduct.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The symmetric coproduct and counit
notes: \(\Delta H=H\otimes1+1\otimes H\), \(\Delta X^\pm=X^\pm\otimes q^{H/4}+q^{-H/4}\otimes X^\pm\); this is an algebra homomorphism and coassociative.
statement: Put \(L=e^{hH/4}\), so \(\Delta L=L\otimes L\). The displayed coproduct extends to the completed algebra, is coassociative, and has counit \(\epsilon(H)=\epsilon(X^\pm)=0\), \(\epsilon(1)=1\).
reconstruction: All tensor products use the same h-adic completion.
fate: These formulas are \citet[I, Theorem~1.1, equations~(1.4)--(1.5)]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi}. Coassociativity on \(X\) follows by expanding both sides as \(X\otimes L\otimes L+L^{-1}\otimes X\otimes L+L^{-1}\otimes L^{-1}\otimes X\). The corresponding pre-seminar structure is also explicit in \citet[Example~6.2, p.~807]{drinfeld1987quantum} (1986 lecture; 1987 publication).
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The antipode needs a minus sign and half the exponent
notes: The scan states \(S(X^\pm)=q^{H/2}X^\pm q^{-H/2}\), with \(S(H)=-H\).
statement: For the displayed coproduct, \(S(X^\pm)=-L X^\pm L^{-1}=-q^{\pm1/2}X^\pm\), where \(L=q^{H/4}\). Indeed \(m(S\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta X=S(X)L+LX=0\). The source expression fails this identity and has the wrong classical limit.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{}
fate: \citet[I, Theorem~1.1, equation~(1.6), with \(\rho=H/2\)]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi} confirms the normalization. The correction is to a faithfully transcribed formula.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the corrected antipode is established; the printed one is incompatible with the printed coproduct.

title: The Cartan-generator substitution changes the denominator
notes: After putting \(K=q^{H/2}\), the notes keep \(KX^\pm=q^{\pm1}X^\pm K\), but write the commutator denominator \(q-q^{-1}\).
statement: With the unchanged parameter \(q=e^h\), the initial relation becomes \([X^+,X^-]=(K-K^{-1})/(q^{1/2}-q^{-1/2})\). If instead the standard parameter is \(t=q^{1/2}\), then \(KX^\pm=t^{\pm2}X^\pm K\) and the denominator is \(t-t^{-1}\). A rescaling of generators is another possible convention, but must be stated.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The correction keeps the original generators and parameter; no silent rescaling is made.
fate: Compare the fixed relation in \citet[I, equation~(1.2)]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi}. Direct substitution detects the factor mismatch.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Finite-dimensional spin representations and the classical limit
notes: \((X^+)^*=X^-\), \(H^*=H\), and a square-root formula is given on \(e_m^j\), with dimension \(2j+1\); Gelfand asks for the \(q=1\) limit.
statement: For real \(q>0\), define \([a]=(q^{a/2}-q^{-a/2})/(q^{1/2}-q^{-1/2})\), with its limiting value at 1. For \(j\in\frac12\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\), \(m=-j,-j+1,\ldots,j\), let \(He_m=2me_m\) and \(X^\pm e_m=\sqrt{[j\mp m][j\pm m+1]}e_{m\pm1}\). These give the compact real-form spin modules and tend to the usual \(\mathfrak{su}_2\) formulas as \(q\to1\).
reconstruction: Nonnegative half-integer j, unit steps for m, and a positive real parameter for the unitary interpretation are restored.
fate: The highest-weight framework is \citet[I, Propositions~1.1--1.2]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi}; the rank-one coefficients can be checked by substitution into the relations.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Expanding vector fields on the sphere
notes: Gelfand asks how to expand vector fields on a sphere in spherical harmonics, beginning with \(SU(2)\). The last word is partly unclear.
statement: For the standard oriented round \(S^2\), a smooth tangent field is expanded in \(\nabla_{S^2}Y_{\ell m}\) and \(n\times\nabla_{S^2}Y_{\ell m}\), \(\ell\geq1\). There is no harmonic one-form term because \(H^1(S^2)=0\). For an ambient \(\mathbb R^3\)-valued field also include the radial terms \(nY_{\ell m}\). Smooth expansions converge in the smooth topology with the usual coefficient decay.
reconstruction: The standard round sphere and tangent/ambient distinction are supplied; they are not explicit in the abbreviated question.
fate: The scalar normalization is given in \citet[\S14.30]{nist2026dlmf}; gradient and rotated-gradient components follow from the Hodge decomposition on the sphere. This answers a classical exercise, not a new quantum-group problem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The universal R series needs deformation factors and a completion
notes: The formula has \(R=e^{hH\otimes H/4}\sum_{n\geq0}q^n e^n\otimes f^n/[n]_q!\), with \(e=q^{H/4}X^+\), \(f=q^{-H/4}X^-\).
statement: The formal quasitriangular structure has \(R\in U_h\widehat\otimes U_h\), \(R\equiv1\pmod h\), and intertwines the two coproducts. Its nth nilpotent term contains a factor vanishing to order n in h, conventionally a power of \(q^{1/2}-q^{-1/2}\). The printed series with the printed e,f cannot have the required classical limit.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The exact missing coefficient is not guessed; only the required deformation order and completion are asserted.
fate: \citet[I, Theorems~1.2--1.3]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi} and \citet[\S3]{reshetikhinturaev1990ribbon} give the quasitriangular construction. The q-exponent depends on generator conventions; this chapter does not invent an exact corrected coefficient from the abbreviated series. The corresponding pre-seminar structure is also explicit in \citet[\S13, pp.~816--817]{drinfeld1987quantum} (1986 lecture; 1987 publication).
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Quasitriangular identities and the Yang--Baxter equation
notes: The intertwining equation and Yang--Baxter equation are stated, but both coproduct-factor identities have their order reversed.
statement: With \(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}(a)=R\Delta(a)R^{-1}\), use \((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})R=R_{13}R_{23}\), \((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)R=R_{13}R_{12}\). These imply \(R_{12}R_{13}R_{23}=R_{23}R_{13}R_{12}\). Opposite conventions require changing the accompanying definitions consistently.
reconstruction: The correction fixes the intertwining convention already printed in the notes.
fate: The stated order is exactly \citet[I, Theorem~1.3, equations~(1.8a)--(1.8c)]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi}, also \citet[equations~(3.1.1)--(3.1.3)]{reshetikhinturaev1990ribbon}. The corresponding pre-seminar structure is also explicit in \citet[\S10, equations~(20)--(21)]{drinfeld1987quantum} (1986 lecture; 1987 publication).
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The q-gamma function
notes: After the q-factorial definition Gelfand asks what \(\Gamma_q\) is.
statement: For \(0<q<1\), \(\Gamma_q(z)=(1-q)^{1-z}(q;q)_\infty/(q^z;q)_\infty\), with \((a;q)_\infty=\prod_{r\geq0}(1-aq^r)\). It satisfies \(\Gamma_q(z+1)=(1-q^z)\Gamma_q(z)/(1-q)\), \(\Gamma_q(1)=1\), and tends to \(\Gamma(z)\) as \(q\uparrow1\) away from poles.
reconstruction: The choice \(0<q<1\) and the nonsymmetric q-factorial convention make the exercise precise.
fate: The standard q-gamma definition and recurrence are tabulated in \citet[\S5.18, equations~(5.18.4)--(5.18.7)]{nist2026dlmf}. The symmetric q-number in the preceding quantum algebra differs by an elementary q-power normalization.

title: Braiding and braid-group representations
notes: \(R^{j_1j_2}=P(\pi_{j_1}\otimes\pi_{j_2})(R)\), mapping the tensor factors in the opposite order, satisfies the braid relation.
statement: For finite-dimensional modules in the chosen quasitriangular category, \(c_{V,W}=P\circ(\pi_V\otimes\pi_W)(R)\) is a natural module isomorphism \(V\otimes W\to W\otimes V\). Adjacent c operators on a repeated tensor power obey the braid relations and define a braid-group representation.
reconstruction: On differently coloured strands one has a coloured braid-groupoid action; an ordinary braid group acts on a fixed repeated tensor power.
fate: \citet[I, \S1]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi} supplies the R-matrix framework; \citet[\S\S3--5]{reshetikhinturaev1990ribbon} formalizes the graphical functor. The corresponding pre-seminar structure is also explicit in \citet[\S10, pp.~811--812]{drinfeld1987quantum} (1986 lecture; 1987 publication).

title: Generic Clebsch--Gordan decomposition
notes: All finite-dimensional representations are called completely reducible, and the tensor product is the classical spin sum.
statement: For a generic parameter, restricted to finite-dimensional type-1 modules, \(V^{j_1}\otimes V^{j_2}\simeq\bigoplus_{r=0}^{2\min(j_1,j_2)}V^{j_1+j_2-r}\). This category is semisimple. Root-of-unity representation categories need not be semisimple, so the omitted parameter restriction changes the theorem.
reconstruction: Generic q and type-1 are specified, and the summation proceeds in steps of one.
fate: \citet[I, Propositions~1.1--1.2 and Theorem~1.5]{reshetikhin1987quantizedi} gives the highest-weight and tensor-product setting. The seminar\textquotesingle s Clebsch--Gordan coefficients are change-of-basis matrices for this decomposition.

title: Graphical tensor calculus, duality, and ribbon structure
notes: Composition joins diagrams; straight strands denote identities, crossings R and its inverse, and cups/caps have signed q-weight formulas.
statement: In a rigid braided tensor category, composition and tensor product are represented by stacking and juxtaposition. Evaluation and coevaluation must satisfy the two zigzag identities; a ribbon twist supplies compatibility with framed isotopy. Explicit cup/cap coefficients depend on chosen identifications with duals and bases, particularly for half-integer spins.
reconstruction: The categorical identities are identified precisely; no unique phase normalization is inferred from the fragmentary coefficients.

title: The coloured link state sum and framing correction
notes: Sum products of matrix entries over spin labels on elementary diagram pieces; multiply by a q-power involving under/over counts to obtain a link invariant containing Jones\textquotesingle s invariant.
statement: The ribbon-category evaluation gives an invariant of coloured framed oriented links. For a blackboard-framed diagram, pass to the zero-framed version by multiplying the contribution of each component coloured by j by \(\theta_j^{-w_i}\), where \(\theta_j\) is its twist scalar and \(w_i\) its signed self-writhe, in a fixed convention. An unweighted under/over count is not the required spin-dependent twist correction. The fundamental \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) colour yields the Jones invariant up to standard variable and normalization choices.
reconstruction: Framed versus ambient isotopy, signed self-writhe and colour-dependent twist are explicit repairs.

title: Other simple Lie algebras and 6j recoupling
notes: Every simple Lie algebra supplies link invariants; 6j-symbols are also mentioned.
statement: For each complex simple Lie algebra at generic deformation parameter, finite-dimensional highest-weight modules and the universal R-matrix yield a family of coloured ribbon-link invariants. Associativity and chosen decompositions of triple tensor products produce quantum 6j change-of-basis matrices, with multiplicity labels when tensor products are not multiplicity-free.
