title: What does sufficiency of the SL2 invariants mean?
notes: There is a conjecture that the \(SL_2\)-invariants suffice; no object or equivalence relation follows the verb.
statement: If interpreted as separation of all oriented knot types by all colours of the Jones polynomial, the assertion is false. But the notes could instead mean recovery of another family of quantum invariants, or another weaker property; the exact conjecture is not recoverable.
reconstruction: The separation interpretation is deliberately conditional and is not entered as the original conjecture in the problem index.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.1]{stoimenowtanaka2008mutation} constructs infinitely many pairs of hyperbolic knots with equal coloured Jones polynomials that are not mutants. The paper records a first manuscript in December 2005 and arXiv circulation in 2006; the opened version is from 2008. This refutes the explicit separation interpretation, not every possible reading of ``suffice.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the exact statement is unidentified; the most natural complete-knot-invariant interpretation has published counterexamples.

title: A rational pole ansatz and its Bethe equations
notes: The Riccati equation is \(y^{\prime}+y^2+2By+C=0\), with \(B=\sum b_\alpha\Delta(\lambda-a_\alpha)\), \(C=\sum c_\alpha\Delta(\lambda-a_\alpha)\), and \(y=\sum_i\Delta(\lambda-\lambda_i)\). The first root equation has inconsistent indices and omits a \(\Delta\).
statement: For \(\Delta(z)=1/z\), distinct fixed points and distinct roots avoiding them, the ansatz solves the equation exactly iff \(\sum_{j\ne i}(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)^{-1}+\sum_\alpha b_\alpha(\lambda_i-a_\alpha)^{-1}=0\) for each i and \(c_\alpha=2b_\alpha\sum_i(\lambda_i-a_\alpha)^{-1}\). Double poles cancel automatically; these conditions cancel all simple poles, and the remaining proper rational function vanishes.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The exact equivalence is deliberately restricted to the rational kernel. Other kernels require additional constant/elliptic compatibility conditions absent from the notebook.
fate: \citet[\S3, Theorem~4, pp.~1197--1198, and \S4]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} develops the analytic pole method, referring back to the author\textquotesingle s 1988 FIAN announcements. The residue calculation gives an exact match in the rational specialization, not an unqualified elliptic theorem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The addition identity and its corrected special functions
notes: For \(x+y+z=0\), \(\Delta(x)\Delta(y)+\Delta(y)\Delta(z)+\Delta(z)\Delta(x)+\Omega(x)+\Omega(y)+\Omega(z)=0\), with odd \(\Delta\) and even \(\Omega\). The trigonometric constant is printed positive and the elliptic expression lacks a half.
statement: Correct examples are \((\Delta,\Omega)=(1/z,0)\), \((\omega\cot(\omega z),-\omega^2/3)\), and \((\zeta(z),(\zeta(z)^2-\wp(z))/2)\). In the last case use \((\zeta(x)+\zeta(y)+\zeta(z))^2=\wp(x)+\wp(y)+\wp(z)\) when \(x+y+z=0\).
reconstruction: \oursComputed{}
fate: The addition identity is classical; \citet[\S23.10]{nist2026dlmf} gives the Weierstrass identity. \citet[\S3 and \S11]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} places such scalar triangle identities in the quasi-exactly solvable construction. Direct substitution checks both emendations.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the corrected examples satisfy the stated equation; the two literal examples do not.

title: A local Riccati identity from the addition law
notes: A solution with a singularity at zero satisfies \(\Delta^{\prime}+\Delta^2=2\Omega+\Omega(0)\).
statement: Assume \(\Delta\) is odd meromorphic with \(\Delta(t)=1/t+O(t)\), and \(\Omega\) even and holomorphic at zero. Put \(y=\varepsilon\), \(z=-x-\varepsilon\) in the addition law and let \(\varepsilon\to0\). The finite part gives exactly \(\Delta^{\prime}(x)+\Delta(x)^2=2\Omega(x)+\Omega(0)\). A different pole residue changes the derivative coefficient.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} A simple pole with residue one and regularity of \(\Omega\) at zero are indispensable extra hypotheses.
fate: The normalization argument for the constant-\(\Omega\) scalar triangle equation is given in \citet[\S3, equation~(27), p.~1197]{ushveridze1989quasiexact}. The limiting expansion supplies the displayed general form.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The claimed general kernel family is underspecified
notes: The general solution is written \(\Delta_0(b\lambda)+a\lambda\), with \(\Delta_0\) one of the rational, trigonometric or elliptic examples.
statement: A valid normalized family is obtained from a residue-one kernel by the rescaling \(b\Delta_0(b\lambda)\) and a linear addition, together with the correspondingly transformed \(\Omega\). A classification of every solution additionally requires regularity, pole and degeneracy hypotheses. The notebook neither gives these nor states the transformed \(\Omega\).
reconstruction: The prefactor b is needed only when maintaining residue one; the original unnormalized family can still satisfy an appropriately rescaled functional equation.
fate: \citet[\S3 and the final elliptic discussion in \S11]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} confirms the functional-equation method, but the retrieved review does not supply an exact theorem with the notebook\textquotesingle s unrestricted quantifiers.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the displayed families are meaningful, but the claimed exhaustive classification is not identified precisely enough to adopt.

title: Logarithmic derivatives linearize the Riccati equation
notes: Putting \(y=f^{\prime}/f\) is said to give a Schrodinger equation; the later page writes \(f^{\prime\prime}+2Bf^{\prime}+Cf=0\).
statement: On an interval where \(f\ne0\), the substitution is equivalent to \(f^{\prime\prime}+2Bf^{\prime}+Cf=0\). Conversely, any Riccati solution gives a local nonzero f by exponentiating its integral. A gauge and coordinate change are still needed to obtain Schrodinger normal form; the first substitution alone leaves a first derivative.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The local nonvanishing condition and distinction between a linear ODE and Schrodinger normal form are explicit.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--3]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} gives the analytic normal-form method. The equivalence follows directly from \(y^{\prime}+y^2=f^{\prime\prime}/f\).
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Electrostatic interpretation of the rational roots
notes: The fixed charges are \(b_\alpha\) at \(a_\alpha\), moving charges are one at \(\lambda_i\), and the potential is written as a positive logarithm. Trigonometric and theta analogues are mentioned.
statement: For real distinct ordered roots and real fixed points, the rational Bethe equations are the stationarity equations of \(U=-\sum_{i<j}\log|\lambda_i-\lambda_j|-\sum_{i,\alpha}b_\alpha\log|\lambda_i-a_\alpha|\). Positive b produces repulsion with this sign. The logarithm of sine gives the trigonometric force; an elliptic force must use a sigma/theta logarithmic derivative with its possible linear term specified.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The real domain and sign convention are fixed. The elliptic theta kernel is not silently equated with Weierstrass zeta without its linear correction.
fate: \citet[\S5, equations~(59)--(63), pp.~1210--1212]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} gives the electrostatic interpretation and real-interval stability assumptions. A positive logarithmic potential with minimization reverses the repulsive-energy sign.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Quantum and classical stability are not an unrestricted equivalence
notes: The same \(\lambda_i\) are called wavefunction nodes, charge positions and Bethe rapidities; quantum stability is asserted equivalent to Coulomb stability.
statement: The algebraic root equations admit these interpretations in the matched model. Spectral admissibility also depends on the Hilbert-space measure, self-adjoint domain, and endpoint behaviour. It is not equivalent merely to existence of a stationary electrostatic configuration.
reconstruction: Only the shared algebraic Bethe equations are identified; physical stability notions require separate definitions.
fate: \citet[\S5, p.~1212, comparing equations~(45)--(46) with (62)--(63)]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} explicitly says the classical and quantum interval conditions almost coincide, with shifted numerical thresholds in that paper\textquotesingle s normalization. Thus the author\textquotesingle s later primary account itself prevents the literal biconditional.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the model-dependent correspondence is established; the unqualified stability equivalence is false.

title: A common eigenspace yields partial exact solvability
notes: For commuting \(H_0,H_1,H_2\), form \(H=H_0+L_1(H_1-c_1)+L_2(H_2-c_2)\). Common eigenvectors with the chosen eigenvalues remain known.
statement: On a common invariant domain, let \(\mathcal V=\ker(H_1-c_1)\cap\ker(H_2-c_2)\) and suppose \(H_0\mathcal V\subset\mathcal V\). Then \(H|_{\mathcal V}=H_0|_{\mathcal V}\). In particular every known \(H_0\)-eigenvector in \(\mathcal V\) remains an H-eigenvector; no commutation of the \(L_j\) with \(H_i\) is needed. A finite-dimensional nonzero \(\mathcal V\) provides an algebraically solvable sector, not the full spectrum.
reconstruction: Domain and invariance hypotheses are supplied; self-adjointness of H is an additional analytic requirement, not automatic from the formula.
fate: \citet[\S9, equation~(113), p.~1232]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} states exactly this operator construction, in a general finite sum. The review appeared in 1989 after the FIAN work cited in the notes.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The nonlinear-Schrodinger and oscillator analogy
notes: Two lines compare quantum nonlinear Schrodinger theory with the harmonic oscillator, and energy with a particle-number operator; spectra are said to come from Bethe equations.
statement: The Hamiltonians, representation spaces, boundary conditions and precise correspondence are absent, so no exact spectral equivalence can be stated.
fate: \citet[\S\S7--9]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} supplies related integrable-spin and quasi-exact constructions, but does not identify these two bare correspondences as written.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: unidentified beyond the integrable-system analogy.

title: The Liouville transform to Schrodinger form
notes: Multiply by an arbitrary A, set \(x=\int d\lambda/\sqrt A\), eliminate the first derivative, and obtain a potential depending on A.
statement: On a real interval with \(A(\lambda)>0\), set \(dx/d\lambda=A^{-1/2}\), \(P=2B\sqrt A-A^{\prime}/(2\sqrt A)\), and \(\Psi=A^{-1/4}\exp(\int B\,d\lambda)f\). Then \(-\Psi_{xx}+V\Psi=0\), where \(V=\tfrac12 P_x+\tfrac14P^2-AC\). Complex versions need a local branch of \(\sqrt A\).
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The gauge factor, positivity/branch condition and derivatives are made explicit; a coordinate change alone does not remove the first derivative.
fate: \citet[\S2, transformation formulas leading to equation~(24)]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} develops the coordinate/gauge procedure. The displayed formula is a direct reconstruction from the notebook\textquotesingle s equation (12).
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Separating a spectral constant from the potential
notes: The product \(A=\prod_\alpha\Xi(\lambda-a_\alpha)\), \(\Xi^{\prime}/\Xi=\Delta\), is said to put all root information into an x-independent energy.
statement: For the rational kernel take A proportional to \(\prod_\alpha(\lambda-a_\alpha)\). Then \(AC\) is polynomial of degree at most \(N-2\), because the Bethe equations imply \(\sum c_\alpha=0\). For \(N=2\) it is a constant energy. For \(N>2\), additional root-dependent coefficients generally remain in the potential and must be fixed to obtain several eigenstates of one Hamiltonian.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} A nonzero scalar multiple can be chosen for positivity on the desired real interval; the source' s bare product may have negative sign there.
fate: \citet[\S4, equations~(38)--(43), pp.~1199--1201]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} distinguishes the infinitely degenerate spectral parameter from the others and makes the N-dependent distinction. The product choice alone does not prove an all-N single-energy separation.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Two fixed positive charges and Jacobi polynomials
notes: For \(N=2\), \(b_1,b_2>0\), repulsion traps M particles between \(a_1<a_2\), giving a solution with M nodes for every M and an exactly solvable model.
statement: Let \(a_1<a_2\) be real, \(b_1,b_2>0\), and \(M\geq0\) an integer. On the chamber \(a_1<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_M<a_2\), the negative-log energy is strictly convex and tends to infinity at its boundary, hence has a unique minimizer. The monic polynomial \(f_M=\prod_i(\lambda-\lambda_i)\) satisfies \(Af_M^{\prime\prime}+2BAf_M^{\prime}+E_Mf_M=0\), \(A=(\lambda-a_1)(a_2-\lambda)\), \(E_M=M(M-1+2b_1+2b_2)\). Here \(B(\lambda)=b_1/(\lambda-a_1)+b_2/(\lambda-a_2)\); for M=0 the configuration is empty and \(f_0=1\). These are rescaled Jacobi polynomials, orthogonal with weight \((\lambda-a_1)^{2b_1-1}(a_2-\lambda)^{2b_2-1}\).
reconstruction: \ours{} The chosen chamber, energy sign, self-adjoint weighted realization and positive A fix the implicit analytic setup.
fate: \citet[\S4, N=2 case, and \S5]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} gives the exactly-solvable and electrostatic interpretations. The convexity and coefficient comparison justify this precise reconstruction; physical boundary conditions after the Liouville transform must still be selected.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Exterior intervals and finitely many admissible levels
notes: For M particles to the right of the second fixed charge, the stability condition is written \(b_1+b_2+M<0\); failure for large M yields only finitely many levels.
statement: With \(b_2>0\), the displayed inequality is a sufficient confining condition for the negative-log energy on the exterior chamber, but it is not generally the sharp threshold. Already for M=1, \(a_1=0,a_2=1,b_1=-1,b_2=1/2\), \(U=\log\lambda-\tfrac12\log(\lambda-1)\) has a strict minimum at \(\lambda=2\), although \(b_1+b_2+M=1/2\). Finiteness of normalizable quantum states requires its own endpoint and measure analysis.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The counterexample only rejects necessity of the displayed condition; it does not reject that condition as a sufficient bound.
fate: \citet[\S5, equations~(62)--(63) and the following comparison, pp.~1211--1212]{ushveridze1989quasiexact} treats stable intervals and distinguishes quantum conditions. The notebook\textquotesingle s conclusion is qualitative; no exact level count or necessary-and-sufficient bound is inferred.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: finite admissible spectra occur in the relevant models; the bare inequality is not a universal sharp quantum bound.

title: The finite-dimensional Morse complex
notes: For a compact manifold and generic metric, trajectories from \(x_1\) to \(x_2\) have dimension \(\operatorname{ind}(x_1)-\operatorname{ind}(x_2)-1\), and signed index-one trajectories define the differential. The vector field is written \(+\operatorname{grad}f\).
statement: For a Morse function on a closed manifold and a Morse--Smale metric, use the negative gradient. The unparametrized trajectory space from p to q has dimension \(\operatorname{ind}p-\operatorname{ind}q-1\). Choose orientations of unstable manifolds; signed counts for index difference one define \(d:C_i\to C_{i-1}\), with \(d^2=0\), and its homology is the ordinary homology. Mod-two coefficients avoid the orientation choices.
reconstruction: Closedness, Morse--Smale transversality, quotient by time translation and coherent orientation choices are stated explicitly.
fate: \citet[\S3, pp.~287--288]{atiyah1988invariants} recalls this construction after \citet[\S2]{witten1982supersymmetry}. The notebook combines positive-gradient notation with the negative-gradient index convention.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The irreducible gauge quotient
notes: The main manifold is \(X=C/G\), irreducible Hermitian connections on the trivial rank-two bundle, with \(G=SU(2)^M\).
statement: Let M be a closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold. On the trivial \(SU(2)\)-bundle, connections form \(\mathcal A=d+\Omega^1(M;\mathfrak{su}_2)\). An irreducible connection has stabilizer the centre \(\{\pm1\}\); after Sobolev completion, the effective gauge group \(\mathcal G/\{\pm1\}\) acts freely and the quotient has local Coulomb slices. Reducible points are excluded from this manifold assertion.
reconstruction: Orientation, completion and the ineffective central stabilizer are restored.
fate: \citet[\S2, pp.~286--287]{atiyah1988invariants} gives precisely the irreducible quotient used in the Casson/Floer picture. The trivial-bundle condition is automatic for \(SU(2)\)-bundles over a three-dimensional CW complex, but is retained from the notes.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The Chern--Simons one-form and its periods
notes: \(\nu_A(B)=\int_M\operatorname{tr}(F_A\wedge B)\) descends to the quotient and is closed. A primitive is identified with a transgression integral on \(M\times[0,1]\); Gelfand refers to Gabrielov--Gelfand--Losik.
statement: For closed oriented M, gauge invariance and the Bianchi identity make \(\nu\) basic. On \(\mathcal A\), a primitive is \(\tfrac12\int_M\operatorname{tr}(A\wedge dA+\tfrac23A\wedge A\wedge A)\). Without the half, its differential is \(2\nu\). With a conventional integral normalization, large gauge transformations change the primitive by periods, so on the quotient the functional is circle-valued or defined on a covering.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} The factor two and integral normalization are distinguished; the notebook suppresses both.
fate: \citet[\S3, pp.~287--288]{atiyah1988invariants} describes the closed one-form, the Chern--Simons functional and its integral periods. The historical Gelfand attribution is recorded as an intervention, not treated as an independent new result.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Flat critical points and the tangent quotient
notes: Critical points are flat connections, hence representations of \(\pi_1(M)\). The quotient tangent space is written with differential forms on X instead of M.
statement: The zero set of \(\nu\) consists of flat connections. Gauge-equivalence classes correspond to conjugacy classes of \(\rho:\pi_1(M)\to SU(2)\). At an irreducible connection, the tangent quotient is \(\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)/d_A\Omega^0(M;\operatorname{ad}P)\), with a Coulomb-slice realization after completion. The base of these differential forms is M, not the infinite-dimensional quotient X.
reconstruction: The notation error X is replaced by M; the tangent quotient is for the irreducible stratum.
fate: \citet[\S2, pp.~286--287]{atiyah1988invariants} states the flat-connection/representation correspondence; the quotient formula follows by differentiating the gauge action.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Twisted first cohomology is not ordinary homology
notes: The Hessian is \(\int_M\operatorname{tr}(d_Aa\wedge a)\). Nondegeneracy is identified with \(H^1(M;E)=0\) for every local system, and then with \(H_1(M;\mathbb Z)=0\). The Russian says \ru{Это эквивалентно}.
statement: At a specified irreducible flat connection with holonomy \(\rho\), the Hessian kernel modulo gauge is \(H^1(M;\operatorname{ad}\rho)\). An integral homology sphere need not have this group zero. Conversely, vanishing of \(H^1(M;E)\) for every finite-dimensional characteristic-zero local system does not detect integral torsion.
reconstruction: The local system governing this Hessian is the adjoint system of the chosen representation, not all local systems at once.
fate: \citet[p.~287 and p.~289]{atiyah1988invariants} explicitly requires perturbations when flat critical points are degenerate. Section~\ref{dev:twisted-h1} gives independently checked counterexamples: \(\mathbb{RP}^3\) for the reverse implication, and the connected sum of two Poincare spheres with an irreducible \(SU(2)\) representation for the forward implication.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the pointwise twisted-cohomology criterion is established; both directions of the notebook' s ordinary/twisted equivalence are false.

title: Spectral flow and the relative grading modulo eight
notes: Index difference is called the number of points where a zero mode appears, then spectral asymmetry; it is said to be well defined modulo eight.
statement: For a path of self-adjoint Fredholm gauge-fixed Hessians with nondegenerate ends, spectral flow is the signed crossing count with multiplicity (or its perturbation-invariant definition), not the unsigned number of zero events. In the \(SU(2)\) instanton theory of an integral homology sphere, changing a path by a generating gauge loop changes this index by eight; hence the relative grading descends modulo eight.
reconstruction: Signs, multiplicities, gauge fixing and the homology-sphere gauge-theory setup are required for the stated eight-periodicity.
fate: \citet[\S4, p.~289]{atiyah1988invariants} gives the spectral-flow calculation and its index-theorem origin. \citet{floer1988instanton} establishes the resulting mod-eight graded homology, received 3 May and published June 1988; only its publisher abstract, not its full proof, was read here.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: A cotangent intersection recovers the Euler characteristic
notes: Take the zero section and the graph of df; intersections are critical points, with signed total written \(\chi(T^*L)\).
statement: For a closed smooth manifold L and Morse f, the zero section and \(\Gamma_{df}\) in \(T^*L\) meet transversely at the critical points. With compatible orientations the local sign is \((-1)^{\operatorname{ind}f}\), and their sum is \(\chi(L)=\chi(T^*L)\), the last equality following from deformation retraction.
reconstruction: Compactness of L, Morse nondegeneracy and the orientation convention are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S5]{atiyah1988invariants} uses Lagrangian intersections as the finite-dimensional model. The equality with the total-space Euler characteristic is harmless here, although the total space is noncompact.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: The closed action one-form and Maslov relative index
notes: On paths from \(L_1\) to \(L_2\), define \(\nu_\gamma(\xi)=\int_0^1\omega(\dot\gamma,\xi)dt\); zeros are intersections, and a relative index is obtained from Maslov theory.
statement: Let \((N,\omega)\) be symplectic and \(L_1,L_2\) Lagrangian. The action one-form on a suitable Sobolev path space is closed because its exterior derivative is the endpoint difference of \(\omega\), which vanishes on the Lagrangians. Its zeros are constant paths in \(L_1\cap L_2\). Transverse intersections give nondegenerate Fredholm Hessians; relative grading uses the Maslov index, with ambiguity determined by the relevant loop classes. Exactness or a covering is needed for a single-valued action.
reconstruction: Lagrangian boundary conditions, Sobolev/Fredholm setup and the action-period ambiguity are explicit; existence of a full Floer homology needs further compactness hypotheses.
fate: \citet[\S5, pp.~292--293]{atiyah1988invariants} describes the symplectic Floer construction and cites Floer\textquotesingle s 1987 preprints. The index formalism has earlier variational background in \citet[\S2]{duistermaat1974morse}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses.

title: Heegaard splitting as a Lagrangian representation-space intersection
notes: A three-manifold is cut into two pieces along a surface; fundamental groups and their representations give the finite-dimensional counterpart of the connection construction.
statement: For a genus-g Heegaard splitting \(M=W_1\cup_\Sigma W_2\), each handlebody group is free of rank g and van Kampen presents \(\pi_1M\) as their amalgam over \(\pi_1\Sigma\). On the smooth irreducible locus, the \(SU(2)\) character variety of \(\Sigma\) has its cup-product symplectic form. The handlebody representation loci are Lagrangian where smooth, and their intersection represents flat connections on M. Reducibles, singularities and transversality cannot be ignored.
